items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the transportation law, in relation to paratransit services
within the state and city of New York during the coronavirus disease 2019
(COVID-19) pandemic
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8119

SPONSOR: COMRIE
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the transportation law, in relation to paratransit
services within the state and city of New York during the coronavirus
disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic

 
PURPOSE:

To ensure that paratransit services-an essential lifeline of many New
Yorkers-continue operating and observe certain public health and safety
protocols for the benefit of workers, employees, paratransit users,
families and the general public.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Amends the transportation law to provide the following:  òPostponement
of Eligibility Expiration. The eligibility of all ADA paratransiteligi-
ble customers, whose certification would otherwise expire between March
1, 2020 and July 31, 2020, shall be extended through at least August 31,
2020 by the relevant paratransit authority in New York State.

* Temporary Suspension of In-Person Eligibility Assessments.The relevant
paratransit authority in New York State shall render eligibility deter-
minations for any application for ADA paratransit submitted before July
31, 2020, based on the application and submitted medical documentation
alone, at least until August 31, 2020.

* Individual Trip Scheduling. Through at least July 31, 2020, all para-
transit authorities in New York State shall suspend shared rides and
shall instead dispatch and route individual paratransit trips, to the
maximum extent possible. Customers shall be notified in advance in the
event that their ride will be shared with another customer, and those
customers shall have the right to refuse or reschedule shared rides
without penalty.

* Virus Protection Measures. All paratransit authorities in New York
State and their contractors will ensure that all paratransit drivers and
personnel providing paratransit services are provided with hand sanitiz-
er, disposable sterile gloves, and training on preventive measures to
protect both customers and drivers from COVID-19 and other infectious
diseases, consistent with current CDC and NYSDOH guidelines.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The coronavirus disease epidemic has changed all aspects of our lives;
one particularly vulnerable population are New Yorkers whose only means
of travel is via paratransit services. This legislation enacts a number
of important temporary measures designed to keep the system seamlessly
moving and keep everyone safe.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 54
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 8119-C, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the transportation law, in relation to paratransit
      services within the state and city of New York during the  corona-
      virus (COVID-19) pandemic"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This  bill,  while  laudable  in its goal of ensuring safe paratransit
access for eligible customers, is  ultimately  an  unacceptable  service
mandate  on  the  MTA  and  other  transit  providers that deprives such
providers with the flexibility needed to control their  own  budgets  in
the  best  interests of the riding public. Each of the measures proposed
in the bill carries a significant fiscal obligation, and while it is  in
the  best  interest  of  the  public  to  administratively implement and
continue these changes for  as  long  as  safety  necessitates,  transit
providers  should  be able to make adjustments at such times as they are
no longer necessary. Statutory time frames do not provide the  necessary
flexibility to ensure proper stewardship of transit provider funding.
 
  Equally  importantly, the MTA and other transit providers have already
acted proactively to implement the provisions of this bill in  a  manner
that  eliminates  potential  fiscal complications. For example, the bill
would extend paratransit eligibility until August 31, 2020  for  persons
whose  certifications  would  otherwise expire between March 1, 2020 and
July 1, 2020. Anticipating difficulties that paratransit customers would
encounter renewing eligibility during  the  COVID-19  pandemic,  transit
providers  have proactively extended expiring designations for sixty day
increments, and will continue to do so for the duration  of  the  public
health emergency.
 
  The  MTA  and other transit providers have also acted proactively with
respect to the other provisions of this bill, including: the removal  of
the in-person assessment of paratransit eligibility (currently suspended
until  further  notice);  the  suspension  of  shared  paratransit rides
(currently suspended until further notice) and the requirement that  all
paratransit  contractors  be  equipped  with  hand sanitizer, gloves and
facemasks (required by Executive Order 202.18). It is also worth  noting
that,  with  regards to the removal of the in-person eligibility assess-
ment, the MTA and other transit providers  have  made  such  eligibility
temporary  only  for  the  duration  of  the public health emergency and
intend on reverting to the established practice when the  public  health
emergency subsides, and have not extended it for a full five-year term.

  As  provisions of this bill are either unworkable or have already been
implemented, the bill is disapproved.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
